cohort: The study included 38 preadolescents (ages 9-13 years), 19 born late preterm and 19 born at term, without access to advanced neonatal care, recruited from a low socioeconomic status community in Brazil.
finding: Late preterm preadolescents showed altered functional connectivity within the posterior default mode networks and increased anti-correlation with the central-executive network compared to term-born preadolescents, despite no significant differences in neurocognitive testing.
